title: Children from Transnational Families Receiving Learning Support or Enrolled in Special Education Schools
what_it_is: Children from Transnational Families Receiving Learning Support or Enrolled in Special Education Schools

sections.label: Transnational families learning support
sections.summary: 129 of about 6,000 students in SPED schools are from transnational families; schools overcome language barriers without monitoring such numbers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) how many children from transnational families are currently receiving additional learning support or are enrolled in special education schools; and (b) whether language interpreters are engaged to support both the Singaporean and foreign spouse in their understanding of their child's additional learning needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: However, we do not monitor the number of students from transnational families who receive the support from schools.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: As at February 2019, 129 students from transnational families out of a total of about 6,000 students attend our 19 Special Education (SPED) schools.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Schools have not reported difficulties connecting with parents even in the minority of cases where one parent may not speak any of our national languages.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Where language is a barrier, they find ways to overcome it, such as enlisting the other parent, other family members, or school personnel who may know the family’s home language.
